_help: Fallback for banks centralbank.watch does not publish probabilities for (it links out to CME FedWatch for the Fed, and omits the RBNZ). Fill hike/hold/cut as percentages plus next_meeting and src. Set "override": true to beat a scraped value. Leave a bank out entirely rather than guessing - a missing expectation is handled, an invented one is not.

USD.src: researched 2026-09-06 (re-check). 4 Sep August NFP printed +162k vs ~53k expected (strongest since March), unemployment 4.1%, AHE +3.1% y/y - a clear beat. CME FedWatch moved to ~58% hike for 16 Sep (Briefing.com 58.2%), interest-rate swaps implied 'above 60%'. Path: ~40% (21 Aug) -> ~57% post-Warsh (28 Aug) -> dipped on the 3 Sep ADP miss -> back to ~58-62% after payrolls. 10 Sep CPI is the last test before the meeting.

JPY.src: researched 2026-09-03. centralbank.watch shows ~58% for a 25bp hike to 1.25% on 17 Sep; Bloomberg (2 Sep) says markets have 'near fully priced' the move after Gov Ueda hinted a hike is likely 'with upside price risks in mind'. Scraper still misses the BoJ block, so hand-entered; nudged slightly above the 58% scrape given Ueda's signal.

NZD.src: researched 2026-09-03. The 2 Sep MPS delivered a second straight 25bp hike to 2.75% (unanimous). No hard market-implied figure for the 28 Oct Monetary Policy Review was found; estimate from RBNZ guidance - the MPS projects only a 'chance' of one further hike before year-end, and Gov Breman told Parliament's FEC select committee on 3 Sep the RBNZ 'can probably take some time to assess' how the two hikes are working, pointing to a hold on 28 Oct with the 9 Dec MPS the live meeting for any further move. Tightening bias intact ('hike option firmly on the table').

CAD.src: researched 2026-09-03. The 2 Sep decision held the overnight rate at 2.25% for a 7th straight meeting; the statement leaned on elevated upside inflation risks (CPI ~3% on gasoline, Middle East energy, new US-Canada tariffs) but gave no signal. Kalshi (20 Aug) had the Oct meeting at hold 84 / hike 16 / cut 4; National Bank and Scotiabank forecast an October hike to 2.50%, while a majority of economists still see a hold through 2026.

_note_CAD: Rate-odds source rotated to public reporting after bankofcanadaodds.com; the TradingView scrape carries a stale 5.25% BoC rate and no real BoC block, so override stays true. If a cleaner current feed appears, prefer it.
